sentences.text: The premaxillae of Morturneria each bore at least eight teeth that were pointed outwards and interlocked rather than directed downwards.
A prominent bend in the frontal bone flared outwards, which may have served to protect the eye.
This extinct genus of plesiosaur was found in what is now Antarctica.
Its unique tooth arrangement suggests it could filter-feed by scooping sand and ejecting water to prey on tiny organisms like amphipods.
Sankar Chatterjee and Bryan Small originally named the species Turneria seymourensis in 1989.
Chatterjee and Benjamin Creisler published the new name Morturneria in 1994 because the original name was preoccupied.
Morturneria belongs to the parent group Aristonectinae and is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Morturneria lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically in the Maastrichtian age.

A 2003 study suggested that Morturneria was merely a juvenile Aristonectes parvidens due to its similarity. However, a 2017 study led by F. Robin O'Keefe concluded that Morturneria is a valid genus distinct from Aristonectes, despite the holotype being a juvenile.
